items.title: The absolute best Black Friday deals we’ve found (so far)
items.summary: This year’s Black Friday deals have launched in waves over the past several weeks, but now the floodgates have officially opened. You can now take advantage of the lowest prices we’ve seen in-store and online for video games, wireless earbuds, TVs, e-readers, robot vacuums, and s
items.content:
Many of our favorite gadgets and gizmos are cheaper than they’ve been all year, making now the perfect time to shop.

If you buy something from a link, The Verge may earn a commission. See our ethics statement.

This year’s Black Friday deals have launched in waves over the past several weeks, but now the floodgates have officially opened. You can now take advantage of the lowest prices we’ve seen in-store and online for video games, wireless earbuds, TVs, e-readers, robot vacuums, and so much more. We can’t guarantee a deal you’ve had your eye on will last through Cyber Monday; however, if prior years are any indication, most will stick around through the long holiday weekend.

As usual, we sorted through thousands of deals to find the ones truly worth sharing, with an eye for the products and services we’ve tested here at The Verge . With prices up across multiple categories due to RAMageddon, some deals may not seem as big as in prior years. For example, Apple’s latest MacBook Air recently fell to its pre-price hike level for the first time since July. That’s a deal to us, and several other discounts are taking a similar shape. We’ll provide context when possible and keep this post updated throughout the day.

Apple’s AirPods Pro 3 deliver the best noise cancellation and sound quality of any AirPods yet, along with a more comfortable, secure fit and improved water resistance. They also feature built-in heart rate tracking for workouts and support live translations for a handful of languages. Read our review .

You can get an ad-supported Disney Plus and Hulu bundle for $4.99 a month ($8 off) for an entire year. Both streaming services feature a deep catalog of new and classic TV shows and movies, including The Simpsons , Andor , Toy Story 5 , and The Fantastic Four: First Steps .

Anker’s durable travel adapter delivers up to 100W of power and works in over 200 countries. It doesn’t support AC plugs, but it does offer a trio of USB-C ports and a nifty LCD display to keep tabs on the charge percentage.

The Nintendo Switch 2 features a 7.9-inch LCD display, magnetically attached Joy-Con 2 controllers, backward compatibility with most original Switch games, and exclusive titles like Donkey Kong Bananza and The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time. Read our review .

An HBO Max Basic subscription provides access to shows like A Knight of the Seven Kingdoms, The Last of Us, and The Pitt , as well as films like Superman and Weapons. You can get a year of the monthly, ad-supported subscription for $5.49 a month (about $6 off) until December 1st.

Compared to the last-gen base Kindle model (currently $119.99), the Paperwhite is a much better value. It features waterproofing, better battery life, faster page-turning speeds, and a higher pixel density screen that’s slightly larger (7 inches vs. 6 inches)

Do you ever wish you could turn on your coffee maker or hit the light switch without getting up? The SwitchBot Bot lets you do that. All you need to do is stick the inexpensive contraption on a standard button or rocker switch, which will allow you to control or schedule your pet feeder, garage door, and a wide range of other devices from your smartphone.

Sony’s XM4 noise-canceling headphones were so good, the company brought them back with a few minor improvements. They still offer great ANC, a timeless foldable design, and delivering performance nearly on par with Sony’s newer flagships at a fraction of the cost.

The water-resistant Sonos Play sits between the Roam 2 and Move 2, offering a balance of portability and room-filling sound. It delivers up to 24 hours of battery life, with a built-in loop for easy carrying. You can also use it as a power bank and pair it with other Sonos speakers over Bluetooth when Wi-Fi isn’t available. Read our review.

Apple’s latest AirTags feature an upgraded ultra-wideband chip for more precise location tracking, a noticeably louder speaker, and an expanded Bluetooth range. Read our review.

Amazon’s last-gen Fire TV Stick 4K Plus streams in 4K and supports Dolby Atmos, Dolby Vision, and Alexa Plus. It also ships with the redesigned Fire OS and, unlike more recent models, still lets you sideload Android TV apps.

Rechargeable AA batteries are handy until it’s time to charge them. Most wall chargers let you refill four, maybe six, at once. Zepath’s clever solution is to ship them in an easy-to-use USB-C charging case that charges eight simultaneously. The batteries themselves are long-lasting, too.

The P9 is great if you need more storage for your Nintendo Switch 2. The microSD Express card offers sequential read speeds of up to 800MB/s, but only gadgets with a microSD Express card slot can take full advantage of the highest speeds. That includes certain cameras, tablets, and drones with a microSD USH-I slot.

Apple’s 11th-gen iPad is the successor to the previous 10-gen model. It has a new A16 chip and few other changes — and is the only Apple tablet to not support Apple Intelligence.

Peacock is a great way to catch up on a wealth of content from NBC’s various networks, whether you plan to rewatch The Office or catch up on all things Bravo. A Premium subscription also grants access to films from studios like Universal Pictures and Dreamworks, along with live sports and a host of Peacock Originals.

With a 4.3-inch E Ink screen, the Xteink X4 is smaller and more pocketable than any Kindle and Kobo model currently available. It has some drawbacks — it’s limited to TXT and EPUB files — but it’s great for tinkering; it also has a magnetic mount so you can stick it to the back of MagSafe-ready phones.

The Ring 5 is a fantastic entry point for new users. While short on improvements over its thicker predecessor, it’s hard not to appreciate that it manages to deliver similar battery life despite being thinner. Read our review.

items.title: The best Black Friday deals on AirPods, MacBooks, and other Apple gear
items.summary: Black Friday is one of the best times of the year to save some cash on a new pair of AirPods or the latest Apple Watch. After all, the holiday savings can help offset the unfortunate price hikes from earlier this year, when Apple raised the cost of some of its most popular gear.
items.content:
We dug up the biggest price drops on Apple hardware and accessories, from tablets and laptops to chargers.

If you buy something from a link, The Verge may earn a commission. See our ethics statement.

Black Friday is one of the best times of the year to save some cash on a new pair of AirPods or the latest Apple Watch . After all, the holiday savings can help offset the unfortunate price hikes from earlier this year, when Apple raised the cost of some of its most popular gear. Some discounts even extend to recent releases like the Apple Watch Series 12 and touchscreen MacBook Pro , which have dropped to new lows.

In addition to a variety of discounts across retailers, Apple is offering up to $300 in gift cards with select purchases between November 27th and November 30th. How much you get back is determined by how much you spend, with up to $100 available for some iPhone and Apple Watch purchases, and up to $300 for the 16-inch MacBook Pro. That said, in some cases you may be able to save more by buying from other retailers.

The latest AirPods Pro offer improved noise cancellation and richer bass, along with built-in heart sensors that work with Apple’s Fitness app to monitor calories burned across more than 50 workouts. Read our review.

Beats’ fitness-focused earbuds feature ear hooks designed to stay put during even the most intense workouts as well as built-in heart rate monitoring. They also deliver relatively bass-rich sound for their design, along with solid noise cancellation, wireless charging, and AirPods features like adaptive audio thanks to Apple’s H2 chip. Read our review.

The latest Beats Studio Pro feature improved noise cancellation, sound quality, and comfort. They also support lossless audio over USB-C and offer native support for a range of iOS and Android features like other Beats headphones. Read our review .

The Beats 360 are ANC headphones for people who prefer headphones over earbuds at the gym. They’re Beats’ first IP-rated cans, with ear cushions that you can easily remove for cleaning (or style points). They also stay in place during most exercises, while still delivering solid bass. Read our review.

Apple’s most affordable laptop uses the same A18 Pro chip found in the iPhone 16 Pro. It features a vibrant 13-inch display, surprisingly good speakers, and 8GB of RAM, making it a solid option for students and anyone who needs a laptop for everyday tasks. Read our review .

Apple’s latest MacBook Air features an M5 chip and starts with 512GB of storage, with significantly faster performance than prior generations. It’s still an excellent machine despite the higher base price, especially given the battery life and speakers. Read our review .

The Apple Watch Series 12 introduces AI-powered Audio Intelligence features, including sound recognition alerts, Live Rewind, and Siri Recap. It can also track your heart rate every five seconds, even when you’re not exercising, and offers faster charging than prior models. Read our review .

Apple’s latest AirTags feature an upgraded ultra-wideband chip for more precise location tracking, a noticeably louder speaker, and an expanded Bluetooth range. Read our review.

The Baseus PicoGo AM52 is a 10,000mAh magnetic power bank that supports fast 25W Qi2.2 wireless charging and up to 45W wired charging via its built-in USB-C cable. It was one of the fastest wireless chargers we tested, bringing an iPhone 17 Pro Max to 65 percent in an hour. Read our guide to the best Qi2 batteries.

Apple’s 11th-gen iPad offers 128GB of storage — twice that of its predecessor — and runs on a faster A16 chip. It also comes in four colors: blue, pink, yellow, and silver.

The Icemag 3 can wirelessly deliver up to 25W of power to compatible smartphones and up to 35W wired charging via USB-C. The 10,000mAh Qi2 charger can also act as a foldable kickstand, comes with an integrated USB-C cable that serves as a lanyard, and sports a transparent design with colorful RGB lighting.

Designed to pair with a Mac, the latest Apple Studio Display features a sharp 5K Retina display, a great 12-megapixel Center Stage camera that keeps you in frame during video calls, and a good six-speaker sound system with spatial audio. Sadly, it only offers two Thunderbolt 5 ports in addition to a pair of USB-C ports. Read our review.

items.title: Apple Black Friday Deals (2026): AirPods, iPads, MacBooks, and More
items.summary: Save on AirPods, iPads, MacBooks, and tons of accessories for Black Friday.
items.content:
Apple gear goes hand-in-hand with holiday sales. WIRED readers love opportunities to save on MacBooks, iPads, AirPods, and other gadgets—and while discounts on Apple products aren't especially rare, Black Friday deals do usually drop these sought-after items to their lowest prices of the year.

I've rounded up the best discounts on Apple products and accessories below. Everything you see has been hand-tested by someone on the WIRED Reviews team, and every price has been hand-checked ahead of publishing. We'll keep this story updated throughout the weekend.

Be sure to check out our dedicated roundups of the Best iPad Deals , Best MacBook Deals , and Best AirPod Deals for more specific picks.

AirPods Pro 3 are finally, actually on sale. The best wireless earbuds for iPhone owners are usually slightly discounted, but this Black Friday price is a truly good deal worth considering if you're in the market for an earbud upgrade. They're comfortable, have great noise cancelation, and have never been this cheap before.

For over-ear headphone enthusiasts looking to keep thing Apple, the AirPods Max 2 are the best option thanks to their clear sound and top-notch noise cancelation. They're also eye-wateringly expensive and basically never drop very far in price. If you've been hemming and hawing trying to figure out a smart time to buy, we think it's right now.

We especially like these earbuds for working out . They fit around your ear so they'll stay in place while running—something AirPods definitely do not do (at least not for me). They have punchy sound and solid noise cancelation, plus dust and water resistance.

We love this MacBook and think it's the best option for most people looking to buy a laptop of any kind. The only real drawback is its price, but at $250 off for Black Friday, now is a great time to buy. It strikes a balance between price and performance that WIRED editor Luke Larsen calls “unbeatable,” and it manages to do it in a sleek, high-quality build that inspires confidence.

The inexpensive MacBook Neo doesn't drop in price very often, but Black Friday has shaved just a bit off the top ($50). We wish it had more RAM, but otherwise, the Neo is totally adequate for most basic use cases: think internet browsing, office software, video calls, and watching your favorite shows.

The base iPad is the model we recommend most often, and while it is no stranger to sales, it's absolutely worth considering if you're thinking about getting someone an iPad as a gift. It isn't powerful enough to be a work machine, but for browsing, content streaming, and “games on your phone,” it'll do the trick.

In my personal and professional opinion, the Apple AirTag doesn't get enough love. I became an AirTag enthusiast this year and now I have one on my keys, in my car, in my purse, and on my luggage. The four-pack price isn't as enticing as it could be, but picking up a single AirTag for under $20 is a steal. The batteries are replaceable and the Bluetooth tracker can play a loud chime if you're looking for it and can't find it.

You can never have enough wall chargers. This option is tiny and comes in colors that match with many iPhones. It has folding prongs and a single USB-C port. I always keep one around for when my power bank inevitably dies.

This MagSafe AirPods case is rugged and protective, with a magnetic closure that keeps your earbuds extra protected. The optional lanyard comes in handy if you don't have space to spare in your bag or pockets.

These privacy protectors are dead simple to install, and we like that the edges of the glass are slightly rounded. Getting two for this price is a steal—both the clear version and the privacy version are discounted for Black Friday.

This MagSafe wallet doubles as a tripod and is great to have around for emergency fit checks or group photos. I also like it for hands-free FaceTime calls. There's a version with Apple Find My compatibility that is also slightly discounted.

MagSafe wallets can be tricky to use, but this one makes it easy to get your cards out. Simply press them in and the wallet's mechanism will pop them out for you to grab. The look isn't that special, but the functionality can't be beat.

items.title: The wild world of tech in 2027...
Credit card skimming scripts using WebRTC found on popular shopping sites
items.summary: Article URL: https://www.infohawk.com/news/2026-11-27-black-friday-webrtc-skimmer Comments URL: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=50668145 Points: 207 # Comments: 122
items.content:
All the sites we contacted took action; but the larger consumer web ecosystem should be prepared to mitigate these attack vectors

A card-skimming script was planted on the online stores of Lascana, Samsonite, American Tourister, Revolve and FWRD in the week before Black Friday. After our reports to affected companies, all have had the script removed (on November 24th or 25th) ahead of Black Friday. We observed it in action on one of the five websites: Lascana, where it sent our test card's details to a 3rd party. We believe the script was built to take a card number, expiry and security code, along with a user's name, address, phone and email, and send them to malefactors as a user entered their payment credentials. It did this before the store checked the payment, so a card could be taken even if the order was declined or cancelled, and nothing would look wrong to the shopper. Across all of these sites, we do not know how many, if any, shopper details or payment credentials may have been captured.

On November 24, we notified all of the named parties in this article and others, including: Amazon Web Services about the storage buckets serving the script, Cloudflare about the services the malefactor used, the domain registrars, the pixel vendor, the consent-banner provider and the affected retailers and platforms. Lascana replied to us and removed the Quorum pixel from their site by November 24th at 15:48 UTC. Quorum confirmed the identified malicious code was removed from their pixel tracker, and they restored the clean marketing pixel as of November 24th at 21:09 UTC.

Revolve provided this statement on behalf of REVOLVE and FWRD: “On November 25, InfoHawk notified our team of a potential security issue impacting mobile and tablet versions of our websites which we resolved the same day. We appreciate the outreach, and are actively investigating the issue to determine any potential impact.”

* Quorum is an ad-attribution platform that links ad views to store visits and online sales ( quorum.inc ).

† Seers is a cookie consent management platform and data privacy compliance company ( seers.ai ).

This attack uses WebRTC, the technology that allows you to make video calls in your web browser. WebRTC lets a web page open its own channel to another party and pass data (e.g. audio/video packets) over it. It has likely been used (both to load the skimmer and to send the stolen card details out) because security rules and monitoring tools often do not watch this communications channel as closely. For example, Meta briefly used WebRTC in a creative way in 2025 , according to researchers looking at the technology as a compromise vector. This form of attack appears to target mobile devices, and we only saw the server enable the skimmer on checkout pages, so desktop checks and homepage scans would likely not see it. The skimmer's traffic appeared to run through Cloudflare's relay, so it would blend in with the WebRTC traffic and hide its true endpoint.

How the kit is designed to work on a store page, in 7 steps. Only step 4 is an ordinary web request, which a connect-src rule can block; steps 5 to 7 run over the WebRTC data channel, outside connect-src .

The loader gets onto the page through a consent-banner setting, a retailer CDN file, a shared marketing pixel or the store's own HTML.

It loads Insds.js or gtage.js from an Amazon S3 bucket.

It runs only on small or touch screens. The Samsonite version runs on /checkout only.

GET /_cf/ice fetches the relay details, and POST /_cf/rel sends the WebRTC offer, to a brand-named northbridgeads[.]com host.

Every exchange that returned relay details used turn.cloudflare.com . The malefactor's answers listed only Cloudflare relay addresses; through that relay it sends code and receives data.

The skimmer arrives in chunks over the channel, is checked against a SHA-256 digest, then run with eval .

At Lascana's checkout ‡ , the skimmer sent our test card details this way.

‡ This was the only example of live card details being sent off-site that we captured.

Check your recent statements for charges you don't recognize, especially on debit cards. Call your bank or card issuer right away, report the fraud and ask for a new card number. Follow up with a written dispute within 60 days of the statement that shows the charge.

Our understanding of US federal law is that your liability for unauthorized credit card charges is capped at $50, and is generally zero if only your card number was stolen, as in a skimming attack like this one. Debit cards have weaker protections that depend on how quickly you report, so act fast. For more information, see “ Additional resources ” below.

That blocks the two web requests the script needs before WebRTC opens. Without them the skimmer never arrives, whichever file was tampered with.

We saw the skimmer delivered in three different ways across five websites run by different companies, and all of them appear to rely on the same attacker infrastructure. That makes it likely that other sites are affected too, so we encourage online retailers to check their own sites for the signs below.

This attack takes advantage of a few critical design decisions in websites that, if improperly configured, allow malicious actors to broadly deploy and trigger exploits across the open web.

Loading third-party tracking pixels on checkout, payment and login pages is far too common a practice today. Each pixel can run whatever code its vendor's file holds, including a skimmer, and whoever controls that file can change it without the site noticing. Every site should review which tracking pixels load on pages that take payment or sign-in details, who can change those files, and whether they need to be there at all.

items.title: Apple’s AirPods Pro 3 are a whopping $100 off for Black Friday
items.summary: The AirPods Pro 3 are cheaper than ever. Despite receiving an early discount last week, Apple’s latest flagship wireless earbuds are still on sale for just $149 at Amazon, Best Buy, and Walmart. They originally sold for $249, but are commonly available for $199 outside major deal
items.content:
At $100 off, they’re the same price as the less impressive AirPods 5.

If you buy something from a link, The Verge may earn a commission. See our ethics statement.

The AirPods Pro 3 are cheaper than ever. Despite receiving an early discount last week, Apple’s latest flagship wireless earbuds are still on sale for just $149 at Amazon , Best Buy , and Walmart . They originally sold for $249, but are commonly available for $199 outside major deal events. The best price that we’ve previously seen was $169.

It’s a weird situation that, right now, the feature-packed AirPods Pro 3 are the same price as the newer (but less impressive) AirPods 5, which include a wireless charging case. The Pro 3 deliver considerably more bang for your buck.

This model is Apple’s best-sounding, longest-lasting AirPods, and they ship with five silicone ear tips. Compared to the second-gen AirPods Pro, these offer better water resistance (IP57 versus IP54), longer battery life per charge (eight hours versus six), improved noise cancellation, and heart rate sensing through built-in sensors. The case also has Apple’s second-gen Ultra Wideband chip in the case.
